text:
amira: customer reported a strange partial-fragment on immediate SSE reconnect. They see the ending of the previous frame split and then charged twice.
amira: repro attached, they force a hard client kill right after the second data event and then immediately reopen a new SSE. No Idempotency-Key used.

kyle: please paste request_id, model, sdk and a raw capture if available.

amira: request_id=frg-4c33a1, route=/v1/streams/generate, model=redwood-13b-v1, sdk=acme-sdk-js@0.5.4, no idempotency. Raw frames below (timestamps approx):

-- initial connection --
data: {"seq": 14, "text": "...we will bill $12.50 for this month."}
data: {"seq": 15, "text": "Thank you and goodbye."}
<socket reset 1006>

-- immediate reconnect --
data: {"seq": 15, "text": "goodbye."}

jonah: interesting — reconnect only received a small suffix ("goodbye.") instead of the full frame on seq 15. That looks like the token/frame got split at a byte boundary and we replayed only the trailing bytes.

ash_s: two likely sources: 1) server resume logic uses byte offsets or per-frame seq that can point into the middle of a UTF-8 token, or 2) network flush split a multibyte token and our resume chooses the wrong replay start. Either way the client saw a truncated fragment and then the resumed session produced the rest, leading to perceived duplicate billing.

kyle: do we currently emit a monotonic token_id per token that is safe for resume? I think we only have frame seq which may not map 1:1 to tokens.

amira: correct — seq is per-frame. Customers have asked for resume tokens before.

ash_s: proposed immediate mitigations:
- runtime: emit absolute token_id on every data frame and in the close/error frame so clients can request resume from token_id boundary.
- api: document/encourage Idempotency-Key for stream creation; warn in response headers when absent.
- client SDK: add default small jitter (50-200ms) before immediate reconnects and attempt resume by token_id when present rather than a blind new stream.

jonah: I'll run a quick staging test: instrument runtime to split a UTF-8 heavy token across two writes and force-close after the first write, then reconnect immediately to observe behavior with and without token_id.

reconnect-bot: collected trace frg-4c33a1 -> s3://ri-traces/frg-4c33a1-2026-03-17.json

amira: customer also flagged that charges appeared twice for fractional tokens. Kyle, can you check billing exposure for that account and whether we should issue a credit if duplicates are confirmed?

kyle: will correlate token metrics with charges post-repro. If duplicates are full or partial token repeats, we should have a manual refund flow ready.

ash_s: long-term fix notes:
- runtime should maintain per-session write-ahead mapping of token_id -> byte ranges until client-ack is received. On reconnect, resume uses token_id boundaries and server avoids re-sending partial UTF-8 subsequences.
- dedupe on token_id server-side for overlapping reconnects (drop tokens with ids already acked).

amira: I'll open a customer ticket with recommended SDK changes (include idempotency_key, small jitter, resume by token_id) and mark this P2 for now but escalate to P1 if billing duplicates are widespread.

jonah: beginning staging run now, will paste results and trace link.
amira: thanks all. :thumbsup:
